newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia communists see commission on spending cuts.
newsitem.headline: Russia communists see commission on spending cuts.

text.p: Russian Communist Party chief Gennady Zyuganov, said on Tuesday he did not exclude the possibility of setting up a special commission to probe government sequestration plans which will cut budget spending.
"Every point of the sequestration plan has to be analysed professionally," Interfax news agency quoted Zyuganov as saying.
"What they (ministers) are suggesting is an outrage... We need to show they are slashing already thin budget articles."

A concilliation commission would group government representatives and members of both houses of parliament but it would only drag out the process of approving the plan, which would slash budget spending by 108 trillion roubles.
The State Duma lower house of parliament is due to discuss the sequestration plans on Wednesday, but the idea of a conciliation commission is only one of the options on offer.
A member of the Duma's budget has proposed amending the budget law to allow the government to slash most spending without parliamentary consent if revenues fell 10 percent below planned levels.
The law as it stands says the cabinet must present a sequestration law to the Duma if revenues are below that level. First quarter revenues were 59 percent of planned levels.
Duma's Deputy Speaker Alexander Shokhin has said this amendment had some chances of approval.
Some analysts say this option would save the Duma's face if the cabinet goes ahead with the spending cuts and would protect some budget articles.
The government wants to cut spending on "priority items" -- mostly payments in the social sphere -- by 30 percent and most other items by 50 percent.
